simple: the machine-code output of compiling one source file, with blanks still to be filled in.
analogy: a translated recipe card with slips clipped to it.
precise: an ELF file of type REL (on this machine) holding sections of code and data, a symbol table and relocation entries; it is input to a linker, not something you can run.
source: D2 of F2-43 (System V gABI / TIS ELF specification), R1 of F2-43 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a named block of a compiled program, such as "all the code" or "all the zeroed variables".
analogy: the labelled boxes the supplier delivers: recipes, spices, empty jars.
precise: a contiguous part of an object or executable file with a name, flags and alignment; compilers put code in .text, constants in .rodata, initialised variables in .data and zero-initialised variables in .bss.
source: D3, D4 of F1-74 (pending verification; book and specification sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of names an object file defines or needs.
analogy: the page titles on a card, and its "see page X" notes.
precise: an array of entries (24 bytes each in ELF64) giving each symbol's name (an offset into a string table), value, size, type, binding, visibility and section index, or "undefined".
source: D2 of F2-43, R1 of F2-43 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: who may see a name and how strongly it is defined.
analogy: a private note on one card (local), a page title the whole book may use (global), or a "use mine only if nobody else has one" page (weak).
precise: LOCAL symbols are visible only inside their object file; GLOBAL symbols resolve references from other files; WEAK symbols give way to a GLOBAL definition of the same name and may stay undefined without an error.
source: D1, D2 of F2-43 (Levine, Linkers and Loaders; gABI), R4 of F2-43 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an instruction to the linker: "when you know the addresses, put this value at this place".
analogy: the slip clipped to a recipe card.
precise: an entry (in ELF64 with explicit addend, a RELA entry) giving the offset of the field to patch, a relocation type that says how to compute the value, the symbol it refers to, and an addend.
source: D2, D3 of F2-43 (gABI; System V AMD64 psABI) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a constant added to the symbol's address in a relocation calculation.
analogy: "minus 4" written on the slip.
precise: the A in the relocation formula; for x86-64 PC-relative fields that end an instruction it is −4, because the processor measures the distance from the end of the 4-byte field.
source: D3 of F2-43 (System V AMD64 psABI), R2 of F2-43 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a blank that must hold a distance, not an address.
analogy: "write how many pages from here to the price list".
precise: a relocation whose value is S + A − P (symbol address plus addend minus the address of the field), such as R_X86_64_PC32; the result must fit the field, here a signed 32-bit integer.
source: D3 of F2-43 (System V AMD64 psABI; formula from memory, unverified box in F2-43), R2 of F2-43 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the linker's report of where it put everything.
analogy: the delivery note listing which box went on which shelf.
precise: a text file written by the linker (option -Map) listing each output section, its VMA, LMA, size and alignment, the input sections it contains and the symbols defined in them.
source: D3, R2 of F1-74 (pending verification; book and specification sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the file format of programs, libraries and object files on Linux and many other systems.
analogy: the standard layout of the bound recipe book.
precise: Executable and Linking Format, defined by the System V generic ABI with a processor supplement per architecture; one format for relocatable files, executables, shared objects and core dumps.
source: D1 of F2-44 (System V gABI) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the fixed-size block at the start of an ELF file that says what the file is and where everything else is.
analogy: the book's first page: for which oven, start page, where the two lists are.
precise: 64 bytes in ELF64: identification bytes (magic, class, byte order, version, OS ABI), type, machine, version, entry point, offsets of the program and section header tables, flags, and the sizes and counts of their entries.
source: D1 of F2-44, R4 of F2-44 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one entry in the table that describes a named part of an ELF file for the linker and tools.
analogy: one line of the cooks' table of contents.
precise: a 64-byte ELF64 record (name offset, type, flags, address, file offset, size, link, info, alignment, entry size); the loader does not use the section header table.
source: D1 of F2-44, R2 of F2-44 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one entry in the table that tells the loader what to put in memory.
analogy: one line of the van driver's list.
precise: a 56-byte ELF64 record (type, flags, file offset, virtual address, physical address, file size, memory size, alignment); PT_LOAD entries describe file ranges to map with given permissions, memory size beyond file size being zero-filled.
source: D1 of F2-44, R4 of F2-44 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a block of names, one after another, each ended by a zero byte.
analogy: the index of titles; elsewhere a line says "title starts at character 27".
precise: an ELF section of type SHT_STRTAB; other structures store names as byte offsets into it; e_shstrndx names the one holding section names, a symbol table's sh_link the one holding symbol names.
source: D1 of F2-44 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the address of the first instruction to run.
analogy: "start here".
precise: e_entry in the ELF header (AddressOfEntryPoint, an RVA, in PE); for a dynamically linked ELF program the kernel first runs the interpreter named in PT_INTERP, which later jumps there.
source: D1, D3 of F2-44 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: testing a program by feeding it huge numbers of random or damaged inputs and watching for crashes.
analogy: handing the reader thousands of books with torn and scribbled pages.
precise: automated generation of inputs, here by mutating valid seed files, run against a target built with sanitizers so that any memory error or undefined behaviour is detected and the input saved.
source: D7 of F2-44 (sanitizer documentation), R5, R8 of F2-44 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program file format of Windows and of UEFI firmware.
analogy: the hotel's book binding.
precise: Portable Executable images built on the Common Object File Format; COFF is also the object-file format; PE32+ is the 64-bit variant (optional-header magic 0x20b).
source: D1 of F2-45 (Microsoft PE Format specification), R3 of F2-45 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a distance from where the image starts in memory.
analogy: "page 12 of this book", whichever shelf the book is on.
precise: an address relative to a PE image's load base; the run-time address is base + RVA; not a file offset, because sections are aligned differently in the file (FileAlignment) and in memory (SectionAlignment).
source: D1 of F2-45, R3 of F2-45 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: where a PE image would like to be loaded.
analogy: "I would like shelf 140".
precise: the preferred virtual address recorded in the PE optional header; absolute addresses in the image were computed for it (0x140000000 in the F2-45 lab).
source: D1 of F2-45, R3 of F2-45 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an entry saying "an absolute address is stored here; adjust it if the image moves".
analogy: the list of places where a page number was written.
precise: an entry of the PE .reloc table (data directory 5), grouped in blocks per 4 KiB page, each a 16-bit value with a 4-bit type (10 = DIR64) and a 12-bit offset; the loader adds (actual base − ImageBase) to each location.
source: D1 of F2-45, R4, R5 of F2-45 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a fixed list in the PE header that points to special tables.
analogy: "imports on page …, fix-up list on page …".
precise: an array of (RVA, size) pairs at the end of the PE optional header; entries include exports, imports, exceptions and the base relocation table (index 5).
source: D1 of F2-45 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program the firmware itself can load and start before any operating system.
analogy: a book the hotel's own staff can cook from.
precise: a PE32+ image with subsystem EFI_APPLICATION (10), entered as efi_main(ImageHandle, SystemTable) with the Microsoft x64 calling convention.
source: D2 of F2-45 (UEFI specification; from memory, unverified box in F2-45), R5 of F2-45 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a text file that tells the linker which memory exists and where each part of the program goes.
analogy: the floor plan saying which shelf holds what.
precise: input to the linker (GNU ld, LLD) with a MEMORY command describing regions and a SECTIONS command placing input sections into output sections at addresses in those regions, and defining symbols.
source: D9 of F1-73 (pending verification; book and specification sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the linker's "current address" while it lays out a program.
analogy: the shelf position Mr Haddad's hand is at.
precise: the symbol . inside a linker script's SECTIONS command; assigning to it moves the layout forward; each output section starts at its current value, possibly aligned.
source: D1 of F2-46 (GNU ld manual) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the parts in the object files, and the bigger parts they are combined into.
analogy: cards from each cook, and the shelf they are filed on.
precise: a linker-script output section statement such as .text : { *(.text .text.*) } collects matching input sections from all input files, in command-line order, into one output section; unmatched input sections become orphans placed by default rules.
source: D1 of F2-46, R1 of F2-46 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the address where code will run, and the address where it is first loaded.
analogy: the shelf where a box will be used, and the loading bay where the van drops it.
precise: virtual memory address (used for every address computed in the code) and load memory address (the ELF program header's physical address); they differ when AT(...) is used, as in a kernel loaded low that runs high after paging is enabled.
source: D1 of F2-46, R3 of F2-46 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a name a linker script defines to mark a position, such as "end of the kernel".
analogy: the tag "soups start here".
precise: a symbol assigned in a linker script (__bss_start = .;); it has an address but no storage, so C++ must use only its address, typically by declaring it as an array.
source: D1 of F2-46, R2 of F2-46 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rules that let separately compiled machine code work together.
analogy: the rules written on the kitchen wall.
precise: data type sizes and alignment, calling convention, stack layout, object file format details and, for C++, name mangling, class layout, vtables and exception handling; defined per platform (for example the System V AMD64 psABI with the Itanium C++ ABI on Linux).
source: D2, D5 of F2-47 (System V AMD64 psABI; Itanium C++ ABI) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the agreed rules for where a function finds its arguments and leaves its result.
analogy: every kitchen agreeing which shelf the order slip goes on.
precise: part of the application binary interface: which registers or stack slots carry arguments and return values, which registers a function must preserve, and stack alignment; different for each ISA and operating system (F2-47).
source: D5 of F1-31 (System V Application Binary Interface, AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement; Procedure Call Standard for the Arm 64-bit Architecture (AAPCS64); RISC-V ELF psABI (all tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a register a called function must give back unchanged.
analogy: the knife you must put back.
precise: a register the calling convention requires to hold the same value on return as on entry (System V AMD64: RBX, RBP, R12–R15 and RSP); all others are caller-saved and may be destroyed by any call.
source: D2 of F2-47 (System V AMD64 psABI; lists from memory, unverified box in F2-47), R8, R9 of F2-47 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a function's own scratch area in memory, made when it starts and removed when it returns.
analogy: a cook's cutting board, cleared after each dish.
precise: the region of the stack used by one function call for saved registers, local variables and spilled values, reached through the stack pointer or a frame pointer.
source: D5 of F1-31 (System V Application Binary Interface, AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement; Procedure Call Standard for the Arm 64-bit Architecture (AAPCS64); RISC-V ELF psABI (all tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: space just below the stack pointer that a function may use without moving the stack pointer.
analogy: the shelf space right under your hand that nobody else touches while you work.
precise: in the System V AMD64 ABI, 128 bytes below RSP that signal and interrupt handlers must not modify; leaf functions use it for locals; kernels compile with -mno-red-zone because hardware interrupts push onto the current stack.
source: D2 of F2-47 (size from memory, unverified box in F2-47), R4 of F2-47 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: 32 empty bytes a Windows x64 caller leaves on the stack for the callee.
analogy: four empty spots on the shelf reserved for the helper's trays.
precise: in the Microsoft x64 calling convention, the caller allocates 32 bytes above the return address where the callee may spill RCX, RDX, R8 and R9; stack arguments start after it.
source: D3 of F2-47 (Microsoft x64 calling convention documentation), R2 of F2-47 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table of function addresses that makes virtual calls work.
analogy: a card on each dish saying which cook prepares its sauce.
precise: in the Itanium C++ ABI, a per-class array with an offset-to-top, a typeinfo pointer and the virtual function pointers; each object with virtual functions starts with a pointer into it.
source: D5 of F2-47 (Itanium C++ ABI), R6 of F2-47 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: C++ without an operating system or its library underneath.
analogy: a pop-up kitchen stall with no supplier.
precise: a C++ implementation in which programs may run without an operating system; only a subset of the standard library is required and start-up and termination are implementation-defined; -ffreestanding tells the compiler not to assume a hosted library.
source: D1, D4 of F2-48 (C++ working draft; GCC manual) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a compiler that builds code for a different system than the one it runs on.
analogy: cooking in the main kitchen for the stall's equipment.
precise: a compiler configured for a target named by a triple such as x86_64-unknown-none-elf (architecture, vendor, operating system, object format); Clang selects the target with --target=, GCC needs a separately built compiler.
source: D5 of F2-48 (Clang documentation), R1 of F2-48 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a list of functions to run before a program's main code, to build global objects.
analogy: the list of ovens to light before service.
precise: an ELF section (SHT_INIT_ARRAY) of function pointers; compilers put a pointer to each translation unit's static-initialisation function there; a hosted C runtime calls them, a freestanding kernel must call them itself.
source: D3 of F2-48 (gABI), R6, R7 of F2-48 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a hidden flag that remembers whether a function's static object has been built yet.
analogy: a "lit" tag on an oven that is lit only the first time someone needs it.
precise: for a function-local static with dynamic initialisation, the Itanium C++ ABI uses a guard object and, for thread-safe statics, calls __cxa_guard_acquire and __cxa_guard_release, which a freestanding environment must provide or disable with -fno-threadsafe-statics.
source: D2 of F2-48 (Itanium C++ ABI), R4 of F2-48 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: type information kept in a program so it can ask "what type is this object really?" at run time.
analogy: a label on each dish naming its recipe.
precise: run-time type information used by dynamic_cast, typeid and exception matching; implemented with typeinfo objects that need the C++ runtime library; disabled with -fno-rtti.
source: D2 of F2-48, R3 of F2-48 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to put a few machine instructions inside C++ and tell the compiler what they read and write.
analogy: a specialist tool plus its handling card.
precise: the GCC/Clang statement asm [volatile] ("template" : outputs : inputs : clobbers); the compiler treats the template as opaque, allocates operands by their constraints and relies only on the declared effects.
source: D1, D2 of F2-49 (GCC manual, Extended Asm; Clang documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a letter that says where an inline-assembly operand must be.
analogy: "put the dish on the left tray".
precise: a string such as "r" (any general register), "m" (memory), "a"/"b"/"c"/"d" (a specific x86 register) or "N" (an 8-bit unsigned constant for I/O instructions); "=" marks a write-only output.
source: D1 of F2-49 (GCC manual, Machine Constraints) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: something inline assembly changes that is not one of its outputs.
analogy: "may splash the counter to your left".
precise: an entry in the fourth list of an extended asm statement: a register name, "cc" (condition flags) or "memory" (memory may be read or written in ways the operands do not show, so the compiler must not cache memory values across the statement or move memory accesses across it).
source: D1 of F2-49, R7 of F2-49 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an instruction only the operating system's kernel may run.
analogy: the oven's reset lever, for the head cook only.
precise: on x86, instructions such as moves to or from control registers, cli, hlt or lgdt that require current privilege level 0 (I/O instructions also depend on IOPL and the I/O permission bitmap); otherwise the processor raises a general-protection exception.
source: D3 of F2-49 (Intel SDM; from memory, unverified box in F2-49), R3, R4 of F2-49 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: device registers placed in the same address space as memory, used with ordinary load and store instructions.
analogy: hatches that look like pantry shelves.
precise: an I/O method in which device registers occupy physical address ranges of the memory address space, so the CPU's normal load/store instructions access them; the address decoder routes those addresses to the device.
source: D1, D2 of F1-41 (pending verification; D1/D2 title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small storage place inside a device that software reads or writes to control it or to ask its state.
analogy: a hatch or a little window in the corridor wall.
precise: a location in a device, with a fixed width and documented bit fields, accessed by the CPU through bus transactions; reads and writes may have side effects (F1-40 showed how the address reaches the device).
source: D1 of F1-41 (pending verification; D1 title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: something that happens in the device because you read or wrote a register.
analogy: taking the tray from the window turns the light off.
precise: a state change caused by the access itself, for example reading a receive-data register removing the byte from the device's buffer, or writing 1 to a status bit clearing it.
source: D1, D7 of F1-41 (pending verification; D1/D7 title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a C++ word that tells the compiler "this value can change behind your back; really read and write it every time".
analogy: the rule "look again each time" for the hatch windows.
precise: a type qualifier; accesses through a volatile glvalue are observable behaviour, so the compiler must perform each one, in program order relative to other volatile accesses; it does not make accesses atomic and is not a CPU memory barrier.
source: D5, R2 of F1-41 (pending verification; D5 title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a field in a PCI device's configuration that says where its registers are.
analogy: the note telling you where on which wall the order board hangs.
precise: one of up to six 32-bit PCI configuration registers (from offset 0x10) holding the base of a memory or I/O region; the low bits describe the region type and are masked off to obtain the address.
source: D2 of F2-50 (PCI Local Bus Specification; from memory, unverified box in F2-50), R1, R2 of F2-50 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
